cards.statement: A perfect non-finite form can show anteriority without using a second finite clause.
cards.explanation: To have and having forms encode an earlier event compactly.

cards.statement: Deny to have copied is the normal pattern for reporting an earlier denial.
cards.explanation: Deny normally takes a gerund, not a to-infinitive.

cards.statement: Having approved the plan can describe an earlier active action.
cards.explanation: Having plus a participle forms a perfect gerund.

cards.statement: Having informed means that the subject received the information.
cards.explanation: Having informed is active: the subject gave the information.

cards.statement: To have digitised is passive when the subject is the archive.
cards.explanation: To have digitised is active; an agent digitises something.

cards.statement: The applicants hope selecting is the passive equivalent of hope to be selected.
cards.explanation: Hope normally takes a to-infinitive in this structure.

cards.statement: Having been approved is an active perfect gerund.
cards.explanation: Having been approved is passive because the subject receives the approval.

cards.statement: Having excluded is passive because the subject receives the exclusion.
cards.explanation: Having excluded is active: the subject performs the exclusion.

cards.statement: To have selected and to have been selected always describe the same participant role.
cards.explanation: The first is active; the second is passive.

cards.statement: Deny commonly takes a gerund, so denied having copied is grammatical.
cards.explanation: Deny having copied reports an earlier action.

cards.statement: To have repaired means that the subject received the repair.
cards.explanation: To have repaired is active: the subject performs the repair.

cards.statement: Claim having found the key is the standard complement in formal reporting.
cards.explanation: Claim normally selects a to-infinitive.

cards.statement: In The bridge is believed to have been repaired, the repair is later than the belief.
cards.explanation: The repair is earlier than the current belief.

cards.statement: To have been digitised marks an earlier passive completion.
cards.explanation: The perfect passive combines have, been and a participle.

cards.statement: Every verb that takes a gerund can automatically take to have plus a participle.
cards.explanation: The main verb still determines whether its complement is a gerund or infinitive.

cards.statement: To have been repaired expresses an earlier passive action.
cards.explanation: Been plus a participle adds passive voice to the perfect infinitive.

cards.statement: Having been informed places the subject as the receiver of information.
cards.explanation: The passive participle shows that information was received.

cards.statement: Claim to have found the key reports an earlier active finding.
cards.explanation: Claim takes a to-infinitive and the perfect form marks earlier time.

cards.statement: To have seen is a perfect infinitive active form.
cards.explanation: It has to have plus a past participle.

cards.statement: To have seen means that the subject received the seeing.
cards.explanation: To have seen is active; the subject performs the seeing.

cards.statement: Been is necessary in to have been selected when the selection is passive.
cards.explanation: Omitting been would remove the passive meaning.
